title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Meconium aspiration
decisions.scenario: A newborn is delivered through meconium-stained amniotic fluid and shows poor respiratory effort.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Ensure airway support and notify the neonatal team.

decisions.title: Hyperbilirubinemia
decisions.scenario: A two-day-old newborn appears jaundiced with rising bilirubin levels.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Neonatal sepsis
decisions.scenario: A newborn becomes lethargic, has temperature instability, and poor feeding.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Notify the provider and prepare for sepsis evaluation.
decisions.trap: Waiting to see if feeding improves.

decisions.title: Neonatal abstinence syndrome
decisions.scenario: A newborn exposed to opioids in utero has tremors, high-pitched crying, and poor feeding.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Implement supportive care and assess withdrawal severity.

decisions.title: Shoulder dystocia
decisions.scenario: During delivery, the baby’s head delivers but the shoulders do not.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Call for immediate assistance and prepare for emergency maneuvers.
decisions.modelWhy: Shoulder dystocia is an obstetric emergency.
decisions.modelNext: Monitor fetal heart rate and maternal status.

decisions.title: Postpartum urinary retention
decisions.scenario: A woman 8 hours postpartum reports suprapubic discomfort and inability to void.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess bladder distension and assist with voiding or catheterize as ordered.
decisions.modelWhy: Urinary retention can lead to infection and hemorrhage.

decisions.title: Rh incompatibility
decisions.scenario: An Rh-negative mother has delivered an Rh-positive infant.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Preterm labor
decisions.scenario: A pregnant woman at 30 weeks reports regular contractions and back pain.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess contraction pattern and notify the provider.
